verdict.script: Image: Latin (Old Irish dictionary with German and English glosses). Transcription and neighbours: Tibetan.
verdict.note: The frame 284 image is an intruder from another book, a dictionary page with entries 'mod' to 'molaim'. The right Tibetan leaf image appears to be missing. The order answer rests on transcriptions: 283 ends 'གྲུབ་པར' and 284's second part opens 'བྱེད་པ་ཅི་སྨོས་ཏེ'; 284 ends 'ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི' and 285 opens 'སངས་རྒྱས'. The first part of 284's transcription ends 'དམ་ཚིག་ཆེན་པོ', which does not obviously lead into its second part, so it may not belong next to it; this cannot be checked against the image. Neighbour leaves have small Tibetan marginal notes that may include folio numbers, but they are not legible at this resolution, so they are recorded as null.

Frame 42 is the unnumbered verso half of a folio; its margin shows only 卷十. The text runs across both joins: frame 41 ends 澤多泉在富平縣西十三里東 and frame 42 opens 南入漆沮; frame 42 ends 自坊州昇平縣 and frame 43 opens 北子午嶺出. The neighbours' folio numbers, 二十一 and 二十二, are consecutive; the last stroke of 二十一 on frame 41 is faint. The toolbar's 42 is a frame count, not a printed number.

The printed numbers run 296, 297, 298, and the text carries across each page edge: catchword 'wir' on 296 opens 297, and 'des an-/dern' runs into 298. The toolbar's 'p. 317' is the frame number, 20 higher than the printed 297. Frame 317 also shows a narrow strip of the facing page's line ends at its left edge, but it holds only one leaf. The signature at the foot of the image looks like 'T 5', while the transcription has 'E 5', which is a misreading.
